code:
Title: Hub-and-spoke topology for HCL's Azure network
Status: Accepted

Decision: Hub-and-spoke; shared services deployed once
in the hub, consumed by every spoke.

Consequences:
+ Shared services patched once, not six times
- The hub becomes a dependency every spoke relies on
  for egress and name resolution
caption: The honest cost of the decision gets written down too, not just the upside.

eyebrow: ADR-003 -- the one that matters most
code:
Title: Shared network services are a DR-in-scope tier
Status: Accepted

Decision: The hub's firewall, gateway, and DNS resolver
are deployed in BOTH regions, with their own documented
RTO/RPO -- at least as strict as the strictest spoke
that depends on them.
caption: Written specifically to close a gap a review board can otherwise miss entirely.

eyebrow: RTO/RPO by tier, not one number

steps.label: Customer Portal: 1hr RTO / 15min RPO
steps.sub: Public-facing; every minute down is visible

steps.label: Dispatch: 4hr RTO / 1hr RPO
steps.sub: Business-critical, but has a manual fallback

steps.label: Shared hub services: 1hr RTO / 15min RPO
steps.sub: Must match the strictest tier that depends on it

steps.label: 1. Fail over Customer Portal
steps.sub: Confirm the 1-hour RTO is actually met

steps.label: 2. Fail over the hub itself
steps.sub: Confirm spokes can still reach the internet and resolve DNS

steps.label: 3. Fail back cleanly
steps.sub: Confirm no configuration drift was introduced

subtitle: A case study of a review board that never asked about the hub's own DR plan.
